question: How did the English word Christmas turn into Kalikimaka when Hawaiian borrowed it?
answer: By being rebuilt from Hawaiian sounds. Hawaiian has eight consonants, p, k, h, l, m, n, w and a glottal stop, and no clusters: every syllable ends in a vowel. So r became l, s became k, and vowels were slipped between the consonants: ka-li-ki-ma-ka. Merry became mele by the same rules.
move: Every listener hears a foreign word through the sounds they already have.
reference: Elbert & Pukui, Hawaiian Grammar, University Press of Hawaii, 1979
